Subject: Urgent: Checkout latency spike + 502s on reserved pool

Sofia —

We're seeing a sustained latency increase and a 502 error spike hitting our checkout flow since ~08:45 PT. This is directly affecting transactions (failed checkouts up ~4.3%). We've verified our traffic is steady and throttling doesn't appear to be on our side. Logs attached (error summary + sample traces).

Key impact:
- Latency P95 for generate calls up from 220ms -> 1.8s
- 502 rate rose from 0.02% -> 1.9%
- Reserved throughput (tokens/s) is returning 40% of expected capacity per dashboard

We need a timeline for mitigation. If you can route us to an alternate pool or enable burst capacity immediately that would help. This is live revenue impact.

— Anika Patel
SRE Lead, FastCommerce
ops@fastcommerce.ai

Immediate asks:
- Ops: can we enable their configured burst capacity for the next 4 hours?

- Sales/CS (Marissa): prepare a concise customer update (what we are doing now + ETA).

From: david_kim@redwood.ai

Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Checkout latency spike + 502s on reserved pool

Sofia — quick triage:
- I pulled the attached metrics. We're seeing sustained KV-cache eviction at an unusual rate coincident with the surge — cache hit rate dropped from 92% -> 58% starting 08:40 PT. That increases decode token work per request.
- Several pods servicing the reserved pool show CPU bound on attention kernels; scheduler is throttling requests which surfaces as 502s in the proxy layer.

Short-term mitigation (next 30–90m):
1) Enable burst capacity to route 25% of traffic to the hosted overflow pool (requires Marissa/CS approval + ops switch). This reduces pressure while preserving reserved SLAs.
2) Apply a runtime flag to increase KV-cache size for this pool by 20% (non-disruptive config flip). I'll push this now — ETA 12m.
3) If the above does not restore headroom, we can route checkout-critical routes to a lower-latency model variant (quantized v2) as a temporary fallback — this requires product signoff (Rishi).

I'll post logs to the Slack thread and attach the quick profiler snapshot. If we need to escalate, recommend a 1:00pm sync with engineering + CS + sales leadership.

— David Kim
Sr. Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: ops@fastcommerce.ai
Cc: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Urgent: Checkout latency spike + 502s on reserved pool

Anika — thank you for the signal and for sharing logs. Quick update from our side:

What we're doing now (summary for your execs):
- We have enabled the customer's reserved burst allowance and are shifting ~20–25% of checkout traffic to Redwood hosted overflow to relieve their dedicated pool while preserving correctness.
- Engineering is increasing KV-cache headroom and monitoring for stabilization (ETA ~15 minutes for initial telemetry).
- If stabilization fails, we will route checkout to a validated fallback model variant with negligible quality regression (we will confirm before cutover).

Request from FastCommerce: please confirm traffic patterns haven't changed (spikes in small-batch queries or background replays) and share any urgent checkout window timing.

We understand the impact to revenue and want to keep you looped. I will send a short executive note we can both use if needed — let me know if your CTO wants a short sync with our VP Sales and CTO.

Best —
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
